answer: I'd like to talk about something small that I keep on my desk at home. A gift that means a great deal to me is a fountain pen my father gave me when I finished my studies. That was when I completed my BBA, just before I started my job at an education consultancy. It is not particularly expensive, but its [[sentimental]] value is enormous. It has a dark blue body with a thin silver clip, and it writes beautifully. He handed it to me with a short note saying he hoped I would use it to sign many important documents in my career. I remember reading the note twice with a [[lump in my throat]]. What made it so special was the [[thoughtfulness]] behind it, rather than the object itself. My father ran a small business for over thirty years, and I think he knew better than anyone how much a signature can carry. My father is not a man of many words, so this gesture was genuinely [[touching]]. I keep it safely on my desk and use it only on special occasions. In fact, I used it to sign my first employment contract, which felt like keeping a small promise to him. Every time I hold it, I am reminded of his quiet faith in me. Honestly, it is the kind of gift that grows more [[precious]] with time. I think the best presents are those that carry meaning and memory, not just a high price tag. This pen is something I intend to keep for the rest of my life and perhaps pass on one day.

followUps.q: Do you still use the pen?
followUps.answer: Yes, but only for important things, like signing contracts or writing Eid cards. I'm quite careful with it, because refilling a fountain pen and cleaning it properly takes a bit of patience.

followUps.q: Have you ever given your father a gift like that?
followUps.answer: Not quite like that, but when he retired, my sisters and I gave him a good-quality watch. He insisted it was unnecessary, but he has worn it every single day since.
